claims.text: What the image looks like Buzzword: pencil-in-cup deformity (DIPs) on hand XR → psoriatic arthritis
claims.quote: Pencil-in-cup deformity (DIPs) Hand X-ray Psoriatic arthritis

claims.text: Common radiographic findings: dist interphalangeal joint involvement; resorption of terminal phalanges and cupping of prox phalanges; arthritis mutilans; and extensive destruction, proliferative bone rxn, a sausage-like appearance to digits, and dislocation of lrg and sm joints
claims.quote: Radiographic findings common in psoriatic arthritis include distal interphalangeal joint involvement; resorption of terminal phalanges and cupping of proximal phalanges; arthritis mutilans; and extensive destruction, proliferative bone reaction, a sausage-like appearance to digits, and dislocation of large and small joints.

claims.text: Main distinguishing features from RA (besides psoriasis): dactylitis, joint asymmetry, dist interphalangeal and sacroiliac joint involvement, and more prominent enthesitis
claims.quote: The main distinguishing features from rheumatoid arthritis, in addition to the presence of psoriasis, include findings of dactylitis, joint asymmetry, distal interphalangeal and sacroiliac joint involvement, and more prominent enthesitis.

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Periph dz may involve sm, medium, and lrg joints, w a tendency to affect dist interphalangeal joints of fingers and toes; patterns incl asym oligoarthritis, symmetric polyarthritis (can be confused w RA), and arthritis mutilans (rapid destructive arthritis w telescoping of the digits); dactylitis, ⍉characteristic of RA, = fairly common and asym
claims.quote: Peripheral psoriatic arthritis may involve small, medium, and large joints with a tendency to affect distal interphalangeal joints of fingers and toes. It may manifest in different patterns such as asymmetric oligoarthritis, symmetric polyarthritis (which can be confused with rheumatoid arthritis), and arthritis mutilans that is characterized by rapid destructive arthritis with telescoping of the digits. Dactylitis, which is not characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis, is fairly common and asymmetric in psoriatic arthritis.

claims.text: Axial involvement may be present, esp in male pts w (+) HLA-B27, and USU manifests as asym involvement of the sacroiliac joints
claims.quote: Axial involvement may be present, especially in male patients with positive HLA-B27, and usually manifests as asymmetric involvement of the sacroiliac joints.

claims.text: Enthesopathy (inflam @ tendinous insertion into bone, eg, Achilles tendinitis, patellar tendinitis, elbow epicondyles, vertebral spinous processes) can develop and cause pain and swelling
claims.quote: Enthesopathy (inflammation at tendinous insertion into bone—eg, Achilles tendinitis, patellar tendinitis, elbow epicondyles, spinous processes of the vertebrae) can develop and cause pain and swelling.

claims.text: Labs: test for RF (occasionally (+)); anti-CCP antibodies are highly specific for RA and only rarely present in psoriatic arthritis
claims.quote: Patients suspected of having psoriatic arthritis should be tested for RF. Occasionally, RF test results can be positive. However, anticyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibodies are highly specific for rheumatoid arthritis and are only rarely present in psoriatic arthritis.

claims.text: Eti A seronegative spondyloarthropathy and chronic inflam arthritis in people w psoriasis of the skin or nails; often asym, and some forms involve the dist interphalangeal joints
claims.quote: Psoriatic arthritis is a seronegative spondyloarthropathy and chronic inflammatory arthritis that occurs in people with psoriasis of the skin or nails. The arthritis is often asymmetric, and some forms involve the distal interphalangeal joints.

claims.text: Develops in ≈ 20% of pts w psoriasis; prevalence = ↑w HIV infect; risk = ↑w HLA-B27 or some other specific alleles (HLA-Cw6, HLA-B38, HLA-B39, HLA-DR) in family members; Eti and patho are unknown
claims.quote: Psoriatic arthritis develops in approximately 20% of patients with psoriasis (1). Prevalence is increased in patients with HIV infection. Risk is increased in patients with human leukocyte antigen B27 (HLA-B27) or some other specific alleles (HLA-Cw6, HLA-B38, HLA-B39, HLA-DR) in family members (2). Etiology and pathophysiology of psoriatic arthritis are unknown.

claims.text: Sx Psoriasis of the skin or nails may precede or follow joint involvement; severity of joint and skin dz = often discordant; skin lesions may be "hidden" in the scalp, ears, gluteal folds, or umbilicus
claims.quote: Psoriasis of the skin or nails may precede or follow joint involvement. Severity of the joint and skin disease is often discordant. Skin lesions may be "hidden" in the scalp, ears, gluteal folds, or umbilicus and go unrecognized by the patient.

claims.text: Flexor tendon inflam may lead to sausage-shaped digits (dactylitis), ⍉present in RA; rheumatoid nodules are ⍉; remissions tend to be more freq, rapid, and complete than in RA, but progression to chronic arthritis and crippling may occur
claims.quote: Inflammation of the flexor tendons of fingers, toes, or both may lead to sausage-shaped deformities (dactylitis), which are not present in patients with rheumatoid arthritis. Rheumatoid nodules are absent. Arthritic remissions tend to be more frequent, rapid, and complete than in rheumatoid arthritis, but progression to chronic arthritis and crippling may occur.

claims.text: Consider in any pt w seronegative inflam arthritis, particularly w dist interphalangeal involvement, asym or lower spine involvement, or enthesitis and/or dactylitis; examine for psoriasis and nail pitting and ask about FHx of psoriasis
claims.quote: Because psoriasis may be overlooked or hidden or develop only after arthritis occurs, psoriatic arthritis should be considered in any patient with seronegative inflammatory arthritis, particularly with involvement of distal interphalangeal joints, asymmetric or lower spine involvement, or presence of enthesitis and/or dactylitis: these patients should be examined for psoriasis and nail pitting and should be questioned about a family history of psoriasis.

claims.text: Tx and next step Tx w DMARDs based on the predom domains involved (eg, periph and/or axial arthritis)
claims.quote: Treat with disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) based on the predominant domains involved (eg, peripheral and/or axial arthritis).

claims.text: Periph arthritis may respond to MTX, sulfasalazine, and leflunomide; hydroxychloroquine = USU avoided (inconsistent benefit; may cause exfoliative derm or aggravate psoriasis); other effective agents incl apremilast, TNF inhibitors, IL-17 inhibitors, IL-12/23 inhibitors, an IL-23 inhibitor, JAK-is, and abatacept; TNF inhibitors are particularly effective for both joint and skin dz
claims.quote: Peripheral arthritis may respond to nonbiologic therapies including methotrexate, sulfasalazine, and leflunomide. Hydroxychloroquine is inconsistently of benefit and may cause exfoliative dermatitis or aggravate underlying psoriasis and is usually avoided. Other effective agents for peripheral arthritis include apremilast, TNF inhibitors, IL-17 inhibitors (eg, secukinumab, ixekizumab, bimekizumab), an IL-12/23 inhibitor (eg, ustekinumab, guselkumab), an IL-23 inhibitor (guselkumab), JAK inhibitors (eg, tofacitinib), and a cytotoxic T lymphocyte–associated antigen 4 (CTLA4) immunoglobulin inhibitor (abatacept). TNF inhibitors are particularly effective for both joint and skin disease.

claims.text: Axial involvement: TNF inhibitors, IL-17 inhibitors, and JAK-is
claims.quote: Therapeutic options for axial involvement include TNF inhibitors, IL-17 inhibitors, and JAK inhibitors.

claims.text: TNF inhibitors reduce the progression of joint damage; they occasionally paradoxically trigger psoriaform rxns (plaque, palmoplantar pustular, and guttate psoriasis)
claims.quote: TNF inhibitors (eg, adalimumab, etanercept, golimumab, certolizumab pegol, infliximab, and their biosimilars) reduce the progression of joint damage (6). TNF inhibitors occasionally paradoxically trigger psoriaform reactions including plaque, palmoplantar pustular, and guttate psoriasis.
